result: Approximate second-order optimizers tend to land in very sharp minima and generalize worse. SASSHA preconditions a SAM gradient with the square root of |diag H| (lazily updated), which makes sharp minima unstable; it finds flatter solutions with better accuracy than first- and second-order baselines.
result_plain: SAM gradient + √|diag H| preconditioning (lazy) avoids sharp minima; better generalization than second-order baselines.
